issue.title: Add Cloudflare to Flask Hosting Platforms docs?

summary.text: This is an open documentation request to add Cloudflare Workers’ Flask deployment guide to Flask’s “Hosting Platforms” section. After expressing concern that company-submitted links can resemble advertising, a maintainer said Cloudflare is comparable in scale to platforms already listed and invited the reporter to open a PR and pass along the Pallets donation link; acceptance was not promised.

known_facts.text: The reporter says Cloudflare Workers supports deploying Flask applications and links to a short Cloudflare guide.
A maintainer initially noted that the examples repository linked from Cloudflare’s guide did not contain the referenced example. The reporter later said the omitted example had been merged.

The maintainer explained that similar company submissions had historically been declined because such listings can feel like advertising, while also noting that Cloudflare is at the same scale as platforms currently listed.
The latest maintainer comment invites the reporter to open a PR and pass the Pallets donation link to Cloudflare, without promising any particular service in return.
The issue remains open and currently has no labels.

missing_information: Whether the reporter intends to open the requested documentation PR and pass the donation link to the relevant Cloudflare contact.

similar_issues.reason: Both issues concern Flask deployment documentation for a named hosting provider, but they request materially different documentation changes: this issue seeks a link to Cloudflare’s existing external guide in the Hosting Platforms section, whereas issue 4884 proposed contributing an independently written Heroku deployment tutorial.
similarities: Both concern helping users deploy Flask applications on a commercial hosting platform.
Both propose changes or additions to Flask’s deployment documentation.
differences: The target requests a link to Cloudflare’s existing guide; issue 4884 proposed an authored Heroku tutorial.
The target specifically concerns inclusion in the Hosting Platforms list, while issue 4884 describes contributing tutorial content created for a course assignment.

label_recommendations.name: docs
label_recommendations.reason: The requested change is specifically an addition to Flask’s Hosting Platforms documentation.

draft_reply: Thanks for following up and for correcting the missing example in the linked repository. The current path forward is to open a focused documentation PR adding the Cloudflare guide to the Hosting Platforms section. This invitation is not a guarantee of acceptance, given the concern about vendor links resembling advertising. Please also pass https://palletsprojects.com/donate to the appropriate Cloudflare contact. Would you be willing to open that PR with a concise entry consistent with the existing platform links?
